description: Three.js WebGL framework layer — renderer, camera, lit mesh, animation loop, resize + HMR dispose wired from first render.

buildHints.whenToUse: 3D scene viewers, WebGL games, shader playgrounds, gltf/fbx asset explorers, or any product archetype where the primary surface is a live 3D canvas.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173 with HMR; the rotating cube renders immediately.
All scene setup lives in `src/main.ts` — scene, camera, renderer, lights, mesh, and animation loop in one file; fork cleanly from there.
Add 3D models via `GLTFLoader` from `three/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js`; place assets in `public/` and load with `new GLTFLoader().load('/model.glb', ...)`.
Run `pnpm build` to emit static assets to `dist/` — no server required, deploy anywhere.
gotchas: `import.meta.hot` requires Vite client types — `src/vite-env.d.ts` provides the reference directive; do not delete it or typecheck will fail on the HMR block.
Always cancel `requestAnimationFrame` in the HMR dispose callback; the handle is stored in `rafHandle`. Skipping this causes multiple parallel render loops and runaway CPU usage.
Call `renderer.setSize(w, h)` AND `camera.aspect = w/h; camera.updateProjectionMatrix()` on resize — CSS-only resize stretches the image without updating the projection matrix.
Dispose geometries, materials, and textures manually when swapping scenes — Three.js does not garbage-collect GPU memory. Use `geometry.dispose()`, `material.dispose()`, `texture.dispose()`.
architectureNotes: Single renderer per page — do not construct a new `WebGLRenderer` per frame or per component; it leaks the GL context.
Keep render-loop work pure: mutate transforms in the loop, allocate meshes and materials outside it. Allocations inside the loop cause GC pauses visible as jank.

placeholders.description: Rotating cube bootstrap. Replace the BoxGeometry + MeshStandardMaterial with actual geometry or a GLTFLoader call. Keep the renderer, camera, resize handler, and HMR dispose block.
